title: DeFM: Learning Foundation Representations from Depth for Robotics

abstract:

title: Playing the network backward: A Game Theoretic Attribution Framework
authors: Jakob Paul Zimmermann, Jim Berend, Georg Loho, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek
abstract:

Abstract: Attribution methods explain which input features drive a model's prediction, making them central to model debugging and mechanistic interpretability. abstract:

authors: Zhe Tao, Feiran Wang, Gaowen Liu, Ramana Rao Kompella, Yan Yan

Abstract: Robots need to anticipate how their actions will change the world, since manipulation success hinges on the resulting contacts and object motions. authors: Itai Zilberstein, Ioannis Anagnostides, Arman Kilic, Tuomas Sandholm
abstract:

Abstract: Modern machine learning models are typically trained on data assumed to be representative of the predictive tasks the model will face in the future, but practical datasets violate this assumption. We focus on outcome-dependent truncation in which an observation appears in the training data depending on its label. title: Primal-Dual Flow Matching for Sample-Wise Constrained Generation
authors: Zhengyan Huan, Peter Y. Lu, Shuchin Aeron
abstract:

Abstract: We consider the problem of learning to generate data while satisfying a prescribed \emph{sample-wise} constraint with a user-specified probability of constraint satisfaction. title: KITE: A Knowledge-Injected Temporal Encoder for Time-Series Event Forecasting
authors: Jonas Petersen, Pratik Jawahar, Riccardo Maggioni, Gian-Alessandro Lombardi, Matteo Cozzi, Marek Gajewski, Federico Martelli, Camilla Mazzoleni, Philipp Christian Petersen
abstract:

Abstract: Forecasting rare, high-cost events in multivariate time-series systems is hard because their precursors are seldom observed, so a purely data-driven model has little to learn from. Abstract: We propose NV-Tesseract-AD, a curriculum learning-enhanced conditional diffusion framework for multivariate time-series anomaly detection. Abstract: Machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells are typically evaluated using random data splits, which we show systematically leak information through massive internal duplication. Because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, random splits primarily reward the mere recall of historical data rather than testing true physical generalisation. title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model
authors: Qingwen Lin, Boyan Xu, Shifeng Xie, Zhifeng Hao, Keli Zhang, Ruichu Cai
abstract:

Abstract: Non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting (NAF) enables time series foundation models to predict an entire future horizon in a single forward pass. Despite its strong sequence modeling capabilities, RWKV-7 exhibits long-horizon degradation in our NAF experiments. In this setup, future patches are represented as missing inputs, requiring the recurrent state to evolve across the prediction horizon without new observations. title: Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation
authors: Woosung Koh, Hyunsoo Lee, Kyungjae Lee, Haeju Park, Dahyun Lee, Dasol Hwang, Moontae Lee
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13113v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continual post-training faces a dual challenge of acquisition and retention: models must learn new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge. While Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) mitigates this using self-supervision with in-context demonstrations, it relies on strong in-context learning and instruction-following abilities. authors: Irene Cannistraci, Julia E. Vogt
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13253v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In-context-learning Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) are uniquely suited to scenarios with limited resources or privacy constraints, as they solve new tasks without additional training. However, their architecture consists of multiple transformer blocks, resulting in high computational and memory footprints. Meanwhile, traditional alternatives like Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees (GBDTs) remain highly competitive and run efficiently on CPUs, suggesting that tabular tasks may not inherently require deep architectures. title: Data-Adaptive Mahalanobis Metric Learning for Cross-Head Attention in Transformers

title: CopRoute: Dependence-Aware Conformal Routing for Language Models
authors: Siva Rajesh Kasa, Santhosh Kumar Kasa, Karan Gupta
abstract:

Abstract: Set-based language model routing aims to increase the coverage of the event where at least one model answers a query correctly while controlling the number of inference calls made. title: A small cognitive core explains human behavior at scale
authors: Marcel Binz, Eric Schulz
abstract:

Abstract: Psychology has proposed many principles of cognition. Each, however, was developed in isolation, leaving their combined explanatory power unknown. abstract:

Abstract: Neural networks (NNs), while highly flexible and versatile, are often poorly calibrated. abstract:

authors: Zeru Zhu, Marco Gamarra, Ji Liu
abstract:

Abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. title: A Distributional Framework for Behavioral Characterization and Risk Management of Large Language Models
authors: David Garc\'ia-Lorite, Raul Merino
abstract:
arXiv:2610.12718v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Large language models are stochastic by nature. Repeated executions under the same experimental conditions may produce different responses. We propose a framework that can be applied across the model lifecycle, from task design to residual behavior and continuous monitoring. title: Scalable Learning of Determinantal Point Processes with Kernel-Structured Interactions

abstract:

Numerical experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our method significantly improves this trade-off, achieving better generalization performance with remarkable parameter efficiency.

authors: Pierre Houedry, Romain Tavenard, Nicolas Courty, Romaric Gaudel
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13129v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is a common choice for measuring the discrepancy between time series. It proceeds by finding an optimal warping between timestamps through dynamic programming, which can be slow and is not differentiable. Consequently, several variants have been proposed. Among them, Soft-DTW proposes a smooth formulation of DTW, amenable to gradient computation, while Continuous-DTW (CDTW) introduces a continuous formulation through parametrizable warping functions. authors: Ionut Adrian Rotaru

authors: Mohammad Siavashi, Pascal Schwinte, Ali Banaei, Gerald Q. Maguire Jr., Marco Chiesa, Dejan Kosti\'c
abstract:

Abstract: Agentic workloads resend long contexts that barely change between calls. Prefix caching now skips most of their prefill, yet every request must still be tokenized in full before the cache can even be consulted. Tokenization, a CPU stage long treated as negligible, becomes the largest part of time-to-first-token (TTFT), and a frontend that tokenizes for a whole GPU fleet limits how many GPUs it can feed. GraphTok reproduces the reference token IDs bit-for-bit on GPT-2, Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemma 3, hands short inputs to a CPU engine where the GPU cannot win, and plugs into unmodified vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo. authors: Xu He, Homayoon Beigi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13440v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Recent accent classification systems can achieve high accuracy in standard in-corpus evaluations. However, when speakers overlap between the training and test sets, such results may overestimate model robustness compared with real-world deployment scenarios. This study revisits the robustness of DistilHuBERT-based accent classification by using L2-ARCTIC and multiple external English accent datasets. Abstract: Nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) can be applied to large nonlinear systems with complex objectives while enforcing constraints, but the cost of solving the underlying optimization problems limits real-time application for systems with fast dynamics or many states. authors: Claudio Altafini
abstract:

Abstract: In machine learning, a self-attention dynamics describes the attention mechanism of transformers, and is obtained treating the layer index of a transformer as time index. Even though naturally discrete-time, this dynamical system is most often studied in continuous-time. Scope of this paper is to provide a thorough investigation of the discrete-time version of the self-attention dynamics: a complete classification of its equilibria is given, and their stability properties are studied, in both the single-head and the multihead case. title: Scalable Sparse Autoregressive Variational Inference for Non-Gaussian Spatial Fields
authors: Paul F. V. Wiemann, Matthias Katzfuss
abstract:
arXiv:2610.13656v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Latent field models are essential for spatial statistics, but the posterior distribution of the latent field, even with a Gaussian process (GP) prior, is analytically intractable whenever the likelihood is non-Gaussian. Existing approximations are either too slow or too restrictive for large non-Gaussian datasets. We present a scalable variational inference framework that mirrors the sparse nearest-neighbor autoregressive structure of the prior in the variational family, uses normalizing-flow conditionals for expressiveness, and amortizes all variational parameters via a single shared neural conditioner. Doubly stochastic optimization with reduced ancestor sets achieves polylogarithmic complexity per iteration.

abstract:

Abstract: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. Abstract: With origins in game theory, probabilistic values like Shapley values, Banzhaf values, and semi-values have emerged as a central tool in explainable AI. abstract:

title: On the Approximation Complexity of Matrix Product Operator (MPO) Born Machines
authors: Chao Li, Zerui Tao, Yuchen Cong, Jian Xu, Qibin Zhao
abstract:
arXiv:2605.11471v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Matrix product operator Born machines (MPO-BMs) are tractable tensor-network models for probabilistic modeling, yet their approximation capabilities remain poorly understood in theory. In this paper, we characterize these capabilities from both negative and positive perspectives. As a negative result, we prove that constructing a polynomial-bond MPO-BM approximation to an arbitrary continuous target with bounded KL error is NP-hard. On the positive side, for score-based variational inference, we prove that targets satisfying a log-Sobolev inequality admit polynomial-bond MPO-BM approximations with provable KL guarantees when the loss-induced Hamiltonian is local and has a constant spectral gap. Furthermore, under the same conditions, we construct local importance-sampling estimators and prove that polynomially many local score queries suffice to preserve the KL guarantees.

authors: Md Farhan Ishmam, Minh Pham Dinh, Kenneth Marino
abstract:

authors: Nina Maria Gottschling, Jakob Gawlikowski, Michele Caprio
abstract:

Abstract: Data-driven approaches often face ambiguity in datasets due to sensor or target noise, insufficient information, and noise in the input data. authors: Priyanka Siddappa, Muntaqim Ahmed Raju, Shifat Haider Al Amin, Ruizhe Ma
abstract:

Abstract: Preprocessing is an under-measured reliability risk in clinical prediction: a model can keep a similar AUROC and still change who receives an alert. Imputation quality is commonly evaluated using reconstruction error or aggregate discrimination, neither of which directly measures agreement on which patients are flagged. At a matched alert rate, pipelines with similar aggregate performance can produce different patient lists. abstract:

authors: Angus Hoy, Austin Lutterbach, Jasper Chong, Aman Kumar, Michael J. Smith
abstract:

title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training
authors: Xinyu Luo, Jincheng Zhou, Mengbo Wang, Zilin Shen, Nadia Atallah Lanman, Petros Drineas, Bruno Ribeiro, Brian Bullins
abstract:

Abstract: A prominent family of low-rank LLM optimizers, pioneered by GaLore, performs gradient-subspace projection: at each step, they project the gradient into a low-dimensional subspace and map the update back to the full model. authors: Pingchuan Ma, Rui Ding, Shuai Wang
abstract:

Abstract: LLM agents can now run causal discovery algorithms on a dataset and report what comes out. authors: Jo\~ao Pedro Silveira e Silva, M\'arcio Dorn, Bruno Iochins Grisci
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22898v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In the age of data-driven decision-making, deep learning models have become powerful tools for uncovering patterns and making predictions that influence many aspects of society. However, their broader adoption in scientific and business applications is often limited by a lack of interpretability. Feature weighting methods, which assess the relevance of individual features, are among the most widely studied approaches for improving interpretability. title: On the tradeoff between robustness and geometric accuracy in adversarial training
authors: Rachel Morris, Ryan Murray, Kerrek Stinson
abstract:
arXiv:2610.22955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For non-parametric binary classification in the presence of an adversary, we prove an optimal quantitative estimate for adversarial classifiers controlling geometric accuracy, as measured by the Hausdorff distance to the Bayes classifier, in terms or their robustness, as encoded by the adversarial budget $\varepsilon$. This rigorously shows that robust classifiers sacrifice at most $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ or $O(\varepsilon)$ in accuracy, depending on the regularity of the underlying Bayes classifier. In contrast to prior work on the incompatibility of robustness and accuracy over low-complexity hypothesis classes, our work shows that high-complexity hypothesis classes allow for robust classifiers with precisely quantified accuracy. Our results apply for adversaries determined by any norm on Euclidean space and in both the infinite and finite data settings.

authors: Mohammad Sadeq Abolhasani, Viswanath Ganapathy

Abstract: The current paper introduces the GraphNARX model, a graph-based nonlinear autoregressive exogenous model for structural dynamics. abstract:

Abstract: Language models that read financial news are usually trained on text from the same years used to test them, so a backtest can reward hindsight. Abstract: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has emerged as a prevalent strategy for adapting large pre-trained models. title: Competence-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models
authors: Jize Jiang, Chengxiang Zhai
abstract:

Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation. title: DIFFLET: A Fast Inference Engine for Diffusion Transformer Models on AWS Trainium

title: HydraLLM: Adaptive Width Slicing for Elastic Text and Vision-Language Models
authors: Oscar Kemme, Janek Haberer, Ali Hojjat, Olaf Landsiedel
abstract:

Abstract: LLMs and LVLMs are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous hardware, ranging from data-center GPUs to resource-constrained edge devices. Their fixed-size architectures limit the ability to reuse a single model across deployment settings with different compute, latency, and model-size targets. abstract:

Abstract: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) transactions involve complex interactions among accounts, smart contracts, and tokens. We investigate whether network topology can identify transaction methods that describe DeFi operations. We extract directed graphlet features to classify the 30 most frequent methods. Using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), we further derive model explanations that reveal method-specific graphlet structural patterns.

title: Language steering in latent space to mitigate unintended code-switching
authors: Andrey Goncharov, Nikolai Kondusov, Alexey Zaytsev
abstract:
arXiv:2510.13849v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) often exhibit hallucinations such as unintended code-switching, reducing reliability in downstream tasks. We propose latent-space language steering, a lightweight inference-time method that identifies language directions via Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on parallel translations and steers token embeddings along these axes to control language identity.
